title: Integration of climate risks in the macroeconomic framework
trigger: BNR publishes a research paper and concept note on climate channels in the Rwandan macro framework, formally integrated into the MPC briefing cycle.
rationale: Climate variables (rainfall patterns in particular) already enter MPC discussions informally, and the November 2025 MPC explicitly flagged a climate-negative scenario that materialised. However, no formal published research exists on climate transmission channels in Rwanda's macro framework. Formalising this through a published paper and concept note creates the analytical foundation for A1.2 and A1.3, and positions BNR to meet its NGFS co-chairmanship expectations.

scalable_ambition.advanced: Climate scenarios formally embedded in the Quarterly Projection Model (QPM) documentation.

ta: Short-term specialised (NGFS methodology, peer central bank exchange) and medium-term support (macroeconomic modelling, co-authoring of the paper).

ta_activities.activity: Workshop on climate macro transmission channels for MPC research team
Peer exchange with climate-active central bank (BdF / RBNZ) and research institutions
Co-authoring support for BNR Review paper
QPM climate scenario integration methodology

donor_complementarity: No active TA on this exact angle; IMF QPM work covers core forecasting but not climate channels.

title: Climate-augmented macroeconomic forecasting
trigger: BNR extends its forecasting horizon for weather-sensitive variables by integrating satellite imagery and ESTEEM model outputs into the QPM, with climate scenarios used in MPC forward guidance.
rationale: BNR's current model is capped at a one-month horizon due to meteorological agency limitations; the data science team already uses satellite imagery for agricultural estimates. Adding a medium-term climate horizon would improve MPC forward guidance. AFD's ESTEEM mission (June 2026, floods/landslides) can provide a good starting point to refine this DLI which bridges a tangible data gap and builds directly on A1.1.

scalable_ambition.baseline: Pilot integration of satellite data into one model module.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Full climate-augmented QPM with extended horizon, gazetted as MPC reference.

ta: Mixed — short-term modelling expertise + long-term capacity building for the analysis and research divisions.

title: Greening of monetary policy instruments — feasibility study
trigger: BNR conducts a feasibility study of climate-sensitive monetary policy tools (differentiated reserve requirements, green collateral adjustments), producing an internal concept note approved at Deputy Governor level.
rationale: BNR is managing a live IMF-ECF reform (data-driven monetary policy framework, price-based auctions, exchange rate flexibility). Greening monetary instruments is the highest-profile axis internationally (NGFS co-chairmanship creates expectations) but remains untouched, for legitimate reasons. It is explicitly dependent on A1.1 and A1.2 as analytical prerequisites and is politically sensitive; a feasibility study is the appropriate first step.

trigger: BNR completes a corporate sustainability diagnostic and publishes a Net-Zero Central Banking roadmap, validated by the Sustainability Steering Committee and timed to the July 2026 mid-term strategy review.
rationale: The Strategy Directorate explicitly requested this diagnostic: sustainability initiatives are fragmented across BNR directorates with no coherent roadmap. The July mid-term strategy review is the natural timing hook. The Sustainability Report is on hold pending exactly this exercise. This DLI is the prerequisite for BNR's credibility as an NGFS co-chair and as a green financial regulator.

trigger: The Government of Rwanda issues a Sustainability-Linked Loan or Bond that includes at least one KPI targeting climate adaptation or mitigation, with a defined SPT and independent third-party verification arrangement in place at issuance.
rationale: The World Bank FCI advisory team is co-developing a SLF framework with MINECOFIN–DG Debt. Rwanda accessed the PBG independently but MINECOFIN confirmed its commitment to SLL issuance by June 2027. AFD's Kenya experience positions it as the natural partner to contribute to the co-design of the framework and support the issuance process.

title: National deforestation monitoring as climate finance data infrastructure
trigger: The Rwanda Forestry Authority and REMA operationalise a national deforestation and forest cover monitoring system producing annual, finance-grade data using a standardised and independently reviewed methodology compatible with SLF KPI requirements, voluntary carbon market standards, and REDD+ reporting frameworks, with data publicly accessible.
rationale: Rwanda's NDC 3.0 includes forestry targets but no centralised, finance-grade deforestation monitoring system exists. The IMF Article IV 2025 flagged climate data infrastructure as a binding constraint. This data layer is the prerequisite for the forestry KPI in B1.3, but also serves voluntary carbon markets (actively explored by RSE and the government) and REDD+ registration. REMA and the RFA have the mandate but lack the methodology and capacity.

scalable_ambition.baseline: Satellite-based methodology validated; first national deforestation baseline produced.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Annual district-level monitoring operationalised; NISR publishes environment data report with forest cover time series.

title: Regulatory framework for climate insurance distribution via SACCOs
trigger: BNR issues a regulatory framework authorising and standardising the distribution of parametric climate insurance products through the SACCO network, aligned with the National Insurance Strategy and the National DRF Strategy.
rationale: SACCOs are the natural last-mile channel for smallholder climate insurance; the current regulatory architecture is not adapted. This framework is the foundational prerequisite for B2.2 and B2.3. It builds on the WB-funded MSME Bridge Lending Window and the DRF Diagnostic / National DRF Strategy (GSFF-funded), which identify parametric products as the micro-level layer of Rwanda's risk-layering architecture.
